meta.scope: Maps recovery diagnosis — GBP and on-page first. Eight tracked queries across Feb 6 → May 6 2026, plus competitive read.
meta.focus: A Maps-only diagnosis. We did not analyze GSC or GA4 in this pass — pull both before the next monthly review so the recovery curve has matching traffic + lead data attached.

tldr: The Maps gap is structural, not effort. MIA's Google Business profile primary category is Photography service; five of the eight top-3 dominators citywide run Photo booth as primary (Glam Shots wins 419 top-3 cells with only 15 reviews — the category match is doing the lifting). On top of that, the site footer phone is 786-973-9973 — the GBP's chat/SMS number — while the GBP primary phone is 786-833-7645; that NAP mismatch suppresses the trust signal Google uses to associate the site with the profile. Fix those two before anything else and we expect a measurable lift inside one scan cycle. The 27 templated area pages on the site (random adjective per slug — leading-, famous-, premier-) look programmatic and almost certainly are not earning the trust they need to support the GBP. We're recommending a clean rebuild of the location and service grid with a proper service×suburb matrix — the architecture this market rewards.

headline.h2: Root cause is two GBP-level fixes — not site depth
headline.lede: Across 6 Local Dominator scans Feb 6 → May 6, MIA's average rank sits at 10.69 (weighted across 8 tracked queries) with 46 top-3 cells out of 712 reached. The two highest-intent terms — "wedding photo booth rental" and "360 photo booth rental" — show zero top-3 cells across every scan. Meanwhile, four competitors with materially weaker review profiles (Glam Shots: 15 reviews; Luxe Booth: 11; Captured Fun: 35) all sit at 300+ top-3 cells citywide. Their distinguishing feature is the GBP primary category.

gbp_audit.intro: Twelve elements scored against the eight top-3 Maps dominators in the same market. The two red rows below are the unlock — every other element on the profile is already healthy.

rows.should_be: Photo booth — used as primary by 5 of the 8 top-3 dominators (Glam Shots, 360 Photo Booth Miami Rental, Miami Event Photo Booth, Capture Pod, The Photobomb Booths). Google's category model rewards a literal match to the user query; "photo booth rental" maps to Photo booth, not Photography service.
rows.evidence: Glam Shots Miami (15 reviews, 5.0★) outranks MIA (103 reviews, 5.0★) in 419 grid cells vs MIA's 46 — the variable that explains the gap is category, not reviews.

rows.current: Photo lab · Photography shop · Photo agency · Photographer · Photography studio · Party equipment rental service
rows.should_be: Replace the stacked photography-only secondaries with: Photo booth (if not used as primary), Wedding photographer, Event planner, Party planner. Photo lab and Photography shop hurt category clarity — they pull the listing toward film-developing intent.
rows.evidence: VIP Party Photo Booth (318 reviews, Party equipment rental service primary) holds 310 top-3 cells — the right vertical stack beats reviews-as-volume.

rows.current: MIA Photo Booth - No.1 Photo Booth Rental
rows.should_be: Keep. Includes the head term twice. The descriptor "No.1 Photo Booth Rental" walks the GBP-naming line but isn't a violation under current guidelines (no city, no superlative-with-modifier).

rows.current: 210-word description, includes 360 / Glam / Black-and-White / Roamer keywords + Miami + weddings/corporate/private parties. Covers since 2020.
rows.should_be: Keep. One small upgrade: add the phrase "photo booth rental" twice (currently used once); add the secondary-target phrase "wedding photo booth" explicitly.

rows.current: Roamer · Black and White · Glam · Social · Studio · 360 · plus the umbrella "Photo Booth Rental in Miami" service
rows.should_be: Keep all seven. Add wedding-specific service ("Wedding Photo Booth in Miami") and corporate-specific ("Corporate Event Photo Booth in Miami") so the services list cleanly addresses the two highest-intent query buckets.
rows.evidence: Both query buckets are tracked: "wedding photo booth rental" (0 top-3 cells), "party photo booth rental" (3 top-3 cells on May 6).

rows.current: Women-owned · Latino-owned · LGBTQ+ friendly · English · Spanish
rows.should_be: Keep all five. Add "Online appointments" and "Online estimates" attributes if available — both are surfaced in the local pack UI for service-area businesses.

rows.current: 20 cities declared — Doral, Miami, Hialeah, Kendall, Opa-locka, Miami Beach, Miami Lakes, North Miami, Westchester, Coral Gables, Surfside, Hialeah Gardens, Pinecrest, Bal Harbour, Key Biscayne, Little Havana, Dadeland, Miami Design District, North Beach, South Beach.
rows.should_be: Keep — broad service-area declarations don't suppress Maps for service-area businesses. But: the website should mirror the same cities in dedicated, indexable pages with consistent NAP. Today's site lists 27 area pages — overlap is partial, slugs are random.
rows.evidence: Site URLs use a different city set (Town Park Estates, Granada, Spring Garden, Gladeview, Coral Groves) than the GBP service area — the two layers don't reinforce each other.

rows.should_be: Keep. 24/7 is normal for service-area / event businesses and signals responsiveness to Google.

Out of scope per the client agreement. No action required on our side; if the team adds photos internally, lean toward 360-booth videos and wedding-event shots (the two undersupplied query buckets above).

Keep cadence. The leader (Glam Shots) has 15 reviews — MIA already wins this dimension. Note that VIP Party Photo Booth (318 reviews) is still slipping (-73 top-3 cells in 3 months), so review-volume alone is not the moat.

rows.should_be: Target weekly cadence (event highlights, booth-type spotlights). Posts feed the Updates tab and have a small but consistent ranking effect when paired with category alignment.

connection.intro: Five elements of the website↔GBP handshake. The site is built — 27 area pages, 6 service pages, 60 blog posts — but the bones aren't connected. The most consequential break is the phone number; the rest compound it.
connection.verdict: The website doesn't currently reinforce the GBP. Until the phone number, schema and URL structure match, every link Google follows from the GBP into the site reads as a weak association — and weak associations don't survive a proximity-tied local pack.

rows.detail: The GBP primary phone is (786) 833-7645. The site footer and every service/area page show (786) 973-9973 — which is actually the GBP's chat/SMS number. Google uses on-site phone-number consistency to confirm a site↔listing pairing; today the strongest match is to a number Google catalogs as "Chat".
rows.fix: One global replace across the WordPress/Wix theme: swap (786) 973-9973 for (786) 833-7645 in the header, footer, schema, contact form, and structured-data tel: links. Keep the SMS number only on a dedicated "Text us" button (use the sms: protocol, not the tel: one). Re-submit the GBP after deploy and watch the next scan.

rows.detail: The homepage and area pages return no JSON-LD LocalBusiness or Service schema (verified via on-page inspection). The richest signal MIA could send Google — name, telephone, areaServed, sameAs (the GBP URL + social profiles), priceRange, openingHours — is currently missing entirely.
rows.fix: Add LocalBusiness schema sitewide (in the theme's <head>), with sameAs pointing to the Google Maps CID URL + the six social profiles already in the GBP. Add Service schema on each of the 6 service pages, with provider linking to the LocalBusiness @id. FAQPage schema on the /frequently-asked-questions page. Expected effort: dev half-day.

rows.issue: URL structure — 27 location pages with random adjective slugs
rows.detail: The 27 area pages use a different adjective per slug: /leading-photo-booth-rental-in-coral-gables-fl, /famous-photo-booth-rental-in-douglas-fl, /premier-photo-booth-rental-in-midtown-miami-fl, /highly-rated-photo-booth-rental-in-little-haiti-fl, etc. This is the fingerprint of programmatic-template content; Google's spam systems have explicitly downgraded this pattern across 2024-25.
rows.fix: Consolidate to a clean /photo-booth-rental/[city]/ structure with 301 redirects from the old slugs. Same on services: /[service]/ stays, and add the matrix below.

rows.detail: Today the site has a service axis (6 booth-type pages) and a location axis (27 area pages) but no cell-level pages combining the two. "360 photo booth coral gables", "wedding photo booth wynwood", "glam booth miami beach" — none of these have a dedicated landing page, despite the GBP's primary service area covering all of them.
rows.fix: Build a 6×15 matrix (6 services × 15 highest-priority cities = 90 pages) over 90 days. Each page = ~400 words of unique copy (venue mentions, neighborhood callouts, one local testimonial, embedded GBP map). Internal linking: each cell links to its parent service + parent city + 3 adjacent cells. This is the architecture Maps actually rewards for service-area businesses with category-aligned GBPs.

rows.issue: Internal linking — area pages don't link to service pages
rows.detail: Sampled three area pages (Coral Gables, Wynwood, Midtown Miami): each links only back to the homepage and to the sibling area pages — no in-body links to the 360 / Glam / Roamer / Social / Studio / Audio-Guestbook service pages. The site loses 27 chances per page to flow authority into its commercial money pages.
rows.fix: Add a 3-paragraph "Booth types we bring to [city]" block to every area page with inline links to each of the 6 service pages. Add a reverse block on each service page ("Most-requested neighborhoods"). Implementation: ~1 hour for a CMS template; cumulative ~50 internal links per page.

levers.title: Switch GBP primary to Photo booth + clean up secondaries
levers.summary: Five-minute change from inside the GBP Manager. New primary: Photo booth. Secondary stack: Party equipment rental service (keep), Wedding photographer, Event planner, Photography service (demote from primary to secondary). Drop Photo lab, Photography shop, Photo agency, Photographer, Photography studio — those pull the listing toward film/print intent and don't add ranking value for booth-rental queries. Expected lift: first signal within one scan cycle (7-14 days); meaningful re-ranking within two cycles.

levers.title: Unify the phone number — site, schema, social, citations
levers.summary: Replace (786) 973-9973 with (786) 833-7645 across miaphotobooth.net (header, footer, contact form, schema, all 27 area pages, all 6 service pages, the homepage hero CTA), then submit to BrightLocal / Whitespark / Moz Local citation pushes. Keep 973-9973 as a labelled "Text us" button only (using sms: protocol). Without this, every other signal on the site is being attributed to a number Google classifies as secondary.

levers.title: Rebuild the location grid on a clean URL + content pattern
levers.summary: Kill the 27 random-adjective area slugs. New structure: /photo-booth-rental/[city]/ for 15 priority cities (the GBP's declared service area + the 3-4 highest-revenue suburbs the team can validate). Each page = ~400 words of unique copy with at least three city-specific anchors (venues, neighborhoods, landmarks), one city-tagged testimonial, embedded GBP map, NAP block in the GBP-primary format. 301 every legacy slug to the matching new URL. Reduce the page count, raise the per-page authority.

levers.title: Add the service×city matrix (~90 cell pages)
levers.summary: Six booth types × 15 priority cities = 90 cell pages. Each follows the same 400-word template, swap-out variables (booth, neighborhood, sample venue, testimonial). The grid is the architecture that out-ranks the citywide competitors who only have one Miami page (Captured Fun, VIP Party Photo Booth). Sequencing: 360 + Glam × the 5 highest-priority cities first (the two highest-revenue booth types × the cities the GBP already ranks in).

levers.title: LocalBusiness + Service + FAQPage schema sitewide
levers.summary: Add JSON-LD LocalBusiness to the theme <head> (telephone = corrected number; areaServed = the 15 cities; sameAs = Google Maps CID + Instagram + Facebook + YouTube + LinkedIn + Pinterest + Twitter — all already on the GBP). Add Service schema on each service page (provider = LocalBusiness @id). Add FAQPage schema on /frequently-asked-questions. Validate in Search Console → URL Inspection.

levers.title: Internal linking + GBP posts cadence
levers.summary: Two unrelated low-cost moves bundled. (1) Add a 3-paragraph block to every area page with inline links to all 6 service pages; reverse block on each service page linking to top neighborhoods. (2) Restart weekly GBP posts (event highlights, booth-type spotlights) — small but consistent ranking effect when paired with the category fix in Lever A.

Headline: Maps performance is structurally capped by two GBP-level settings, not by effort or reviews. The fix is targeted, not heavy.

Across 6 scans, MIA averages rank 10.69 on Maps (weighted across all 8 tracked queries) with 46 top-3 cells out of 712 reached. The two highest-intent queries — "wedding photo booth rental" and "360 photo booth rental" — show zero top-3 cells in every scan. Meanwhile, the four competitors who dominate Maps (Glam Shots: 419 top-3 cells with only 15 reviews; Captured Fun: 403 with 35; Luxe Booth: 319 with 11; 360 Photo Booth Miami Rental: 319 with 32) all share two things MIA doesn't: (1) a GBP primary category that literally matches the query — "Photo booth" or "Party equipment rental service" — vs MIA's "Photography service"; and (2) a website phone number that matches the GBP primary number. MIA's site shows (786) 973-9973 sitewide — that's the GBP chat/SMS number, not the primary (786) 833-7645. Two changes (5 minutes inside the GBP + half-day dev on the site) should produce a measurable lift inside the next two scan cycles.
